step_by_step_reasoning: The architecture diagram depicts an internal developer platform ('Orion') built on AWS to automate microservice environment provisioning. An internal developer user accesses the platform via Route 53 DNS resolution, which routes requests through an Application Load Balancer (ALB) to Amazon EKS running on EC2 Spot Instances. When jobs spin up microservices, job status events are published to SNS and fanned out to SQS, allowing replacement spot instances/jobs to poll SQS and complete any interrupted tasks seamlessly.

graph.name: OLX Autos Internal Developer Platform on Amazon EKS and EC2 Spot
graph.notes: The system utilizes 100% EC2 Spot instances managed by EKS, using SNS and SQS for resilient job state tracking upon spot interruptions.

edges.notes: User accesses Orion portal URL routed via Route 53
Route 53 resolves DNS to the Application Load Balancer
ALB forwards provisioning request to EKS
EKS schedules workloads and jobs on EC2 Spot instances
Provisioning jobs send state change events to SNS
SNS fans out job status messages to SQS
Replacement jobs on Spot instances poll SQS to complete interrupted tasks
